change.item: Placement is now the module position you assign in Joomla. The Position parameter (top of the article, floating left, floating right) has been removed together with the script that moved the module next to the article body: it duplicated the module position selector every Joomla module already has. The module renders where the template renders it.

The box no longer has a width of its own. The fixed Width parameter has been removed; the module fills the position it sits in and also behaves correctly as a flex or grid item inside a builder panel or a card grid. Set the size from the position, the template, or the module's Custom CSS field.

remove.item: The "position" and "width" parameters, the "--toc-width" custom property and the placement CSS classes. Values already saved for existing modules are ignored, so nothing has to be cleaned up before updating.

note.item: Modules that relied on the floating placement now appear in their assigned template position. To keep the table of contents beside the article text, assign the module to a sidebar position of the template.
Requires Joomla 6.0 or later and PHP 8.3 or later.

fix.item: The box was unreadable on a dark template: the background colour defaulted to a near white value while the text and link colours are inherited from the template, so light text landed on a light box. Background and border colours now default to empty, which makes the box take the template's own background and gives it a neutral grey border that stays visible either way. Existing modules keep whatever colours were saved for them; clear the two colour fields to pick up the new behaviour.

The module title was left behind when the module moved out of a wrapper the chrome selectors did not recognise, such as the bare panel that the YOOtheme Pro Builder module element renders. A parent now counts as the module's own wrapper when it holds nothing but this module, its title and the noscript fallback.

note.item: Requires Joomla 6.0 or later and PHP 8.3 or later.

addition.item: First public release: a site module that builds a table of contents from the headings of the article currently being viewed, entirely in the browser, with no external JavaScript or CSS dependencies.
Heading levels picked up are configurable (H2 to H6), and the module hides itself completely when the article contains fewer matching headings than the configured minimum.
Three placements independent of the assigned module position: at the top of the article, floating left of it, or floating right of it.
Optional numbered list, collapsible box (optionally collapsed on load), and smooth scrolling with a configurable scroll offset for sticky site headers.
Appearance settings for width, background, border, text and link colours, font size and a custom wrapper class, plus a per-instance Custom CSS field.

Adjustable article content CSS selector, with automatic detection of the article body when the selector matches nothing — this is what makes the module work on page builder layouts such as YOOtheme Pro, which emit no recognisable article markup.

Module chrome is recognised for templates that wrap modules in a card, a moduletable or a "module-<id>" element, so the whole box is moved next to the article; wrappers the moved or hidden module leaves empty are removed with it.
Ships English (en-GB) and Ukrainian (uk-UA) language files, and supports alternative module layouts.

security.item: The Custom CSS parameter is stored unfiltered by design but is sanitised on every render before it is echoed: selector break-outs, braces, comments, at-rules and the legacy script-in-CSS vectors are stripped, so an operator with edit rights on the module cannot inject markup or script into the page.

note.item: Requires Joomla 6.0 or later and PHP 8.3 or later.
